title: Aromaticity
description: Why is benzene so content? Hückel put its six p electrons on a ring of six atoms and solved for the orbitals: one low level, then pairs, so six fill a closed shell. Any ring with 4n + 2 electrons does, and is stabilised; 4n fills a pair halfway and is worse off than an open chain: antiaromatic. The test is a magnet: an aromatic ring's electrons circle in the field, shielding the protons inside the ring and deshielding those outside, so [18]annulene's inner hydrogens sit at minus three parts per million. Unlocks the Hückel Analyser.

puzzle.goal: On a ring of n atoms each joined by β, Hückel theory gives orbital energies α + 2β·cos(2πk/n) for k = 0 to n − 1. Write the energy E of the lowest orbital.
puzzle.name: Hückel ring orbitals
puzzle.form: α + 2 * β * cos ( 2 * π * k / n )
puzzle.expr: a + 2 * b * cos ( 2 * π * k / n )
puzzle.ask: Find E in eV for α = −6.6, β = −2.7, n = 6 and k = @{k}.
puzzle.method: The ring is symmetric under turning by one atom: the orbitals are waves e^(2πikj/n), each atom coupled to its two neighbours.
